speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin our investigation, could you describe the specific activities that seem to trigger these episodes of stridor and wheezing? Also, how old is the infant?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the worsening with neck flexion is a very specific clue. To further narrow this down, do you notice that these episodes occur in a particular position or time of day, and has anyone observed a clicking sound or "click" when you palpate the trachea? Also, have you noticed any cyanosis (bluish tint) during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).
